speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain but no fever. To help me understand your condition, where exactly is the pain located, and when did you first notice the limp?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since he is a 7-year-old male with left knee pain and a limp but no fever or trauma, could you please describe the exact location of the tenderness—is it directly over the kneecap or slightly below it? Also, does he have any history of similar episodes or a family history of bone issues?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Sever's disease (Calcaneal apophysitis). The clinical picture of a limp and localized pain in the left knee (referred from the heel) in a 7-year-old male without fever or trauma is classic for this condition, which is common in active children of this age group.
